newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty slips but remains range-bound.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty slips but remains range-bound.

text.p: The Polish zloty moved lower against the currency basket in early trade but dealers said that the local currency was bound to remain in its four-week range between 2.4 and 2.5 percent from parity.
Dealers said that emerging market investors, whose entry into Polish treasuries has kept the zloty buoyant, were focused on events in the Czech Republic and the crown's decline.

"The zloty has temporarily slipped from its 2.5 percent perch as foreign investors are focused on the Czech crown and orders from (Polish) domestic clients created some currency buying," said Mateusz Bieniek of Societe Generale in Warsaw.
"But this is only a short-term trend and the zloty is likely to remain between 2.4 and 2.5 percent," he added.
At 0830 GMT the zloty rebounded to 2.50/2.48 percent from parity after opening and early treade at 2.46/2.41 percent.
It was at 3.1507/12 to the dollar, up from 3.1540/60 at 0700 and at 1.8525/30 to the mark, down from 1.8515/25.
One-day rates inched up slightly above 22 percent on after the central bank announced a 500 million zloty reverse repo and 200 million NBP-bill sale on Friday.
Overnight rates rose to 21.95/22.05 percent from opening's 21.8/22.0 while tomorrow/next to 21.90/22.21 from 21.8/22.18.

Dealers said money market rates would likely refrain from falling in line with inflation as the central bank was still primarily concerned with cooling credit action and with it quickly growing domestic demand.

"Money market rates are not likely to fall in the near-term...especially after the central bank increased obligatory reserve requirements on term deposits," said Iwona Saszin-Krawczyk, dealer at PKO SA.
Poland's inflation fell to year-on-year 15.3 percent in April from March's 16.6 percent and analysts said that oficial interest rates should be flat until at least the third quarter.
The central bank increased obligatory reserves on zloty term deposits by two points to 11 percent and by one point to five percent on foreign currency deposits as of April 30.
